ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Five points on a circle are numbered 1,2,3,4, and 5 in clockwise order. A bug jumps in a clockwise direction from one point to another around the circle; if it is on an odd-numbered point, it moves one point, and if it is on an even-numbered point, it moves two points. If the bug begins on point 5, after 1995 jumps it will be on point

Odd-numbered points move 1 point: 1→2, 3→4, 5→1. Even-numbered points move 2 points: 2→4, 4→1. So starting from 5, the 1st jump is 5→1. After that it cycles among 1, 2, and 4: 1→2→4→1, with period 3. method.method_draft: Treat movement as modular displacement around five positions. Read the labels as positions in clockwise order 1,2,3,4,5 modulo 5. Starting at 5, the first jump is one clockwise step because 5 is odd, so the bug lands on 1. From 1, examine a three-jump block: 1 moves +1 to 2, 2 moves +2 to 4, and 4 moves +2 to 1, for a total displacement of 5 positions, returning to 1. Thus every 3 jumps from point 1 resets the bug to point 1. Decompose 1995 = 1 + 3·664 + 2. After the first jump and 664 full blocks the bug is still at 1, then two more jumps take it 1→2→4.
